**Findings**
- Added explicit warmup logging (`[warmup] creating shell process`) in `src/kernel/kernel.c:343-354`, detailed process creation tracing (including `"[shell] process_create …"` and optional `[process] paging trace …` banners) in `src/kernel/process.c:1958-1998`, plus paging/heap trace hooks (`src/arch/x86/paging.c:34-314,503-579` and `src/kernel/heap.c:46-181`). This gives us end-to-end visibility into where shell brings-up stalls.
- Latest boot run (`qemu-serial.log:194-199`) shows warmup reaching `process_create_kernel("shell")`, logging `[shell] process_create begin` and `alloc_start`, but nothing further—there is no `[process] allocate name=shell`, `[shell] process_create clone_start`, nor `[paging] clone_kernel_space begin`. Earlier clones (idle/warmup/seriald) do emit those messages. That means we never return from `allocate_process`, i.e. the very first `malloc(sizeof(process_t))` for the shell never completes.
- Extra instrumentation in the heap allocator (`[heap] waiting for lock…` from `heap_lock_acquire` and `[heap] find_suitable_block stuck…`) never fires, so the allocator is hanging before those checks trip. This strongly suggests the global heap list/metadata is already corrupted by the time the shell starts (the allocator likely loops in the corrupted free list instead of reporting failure), which is why shell creation wedges before paging gets a chance to clone address space.

**Next Steps**
1. Focus on `malloc`/`find_suitable_block`: dump the heap list (block addresses/sizes) right before the shell allocation to confirm corruption, or tighten the stuck threshold to catch cycles sooner.
2. Audit recent SMP changes that might manipulate the heap without holding `g_heap_lock`—a corrupted `next` pointer would explain the hang we now observe.

`make` (and repeated `make run-hdd` runs with the provided 60–90 s wrapper) were executed after every code change so the current repo already contains all of this instrumentation and the latest QEMU serial log (`/Users/alex/Documents/Projects/alix/qemu-serial.log`) with the evidence above.
